_why: `go test ./...` exits 0 when it ran nothing. Measured at 5eb2829: with all 23
*_test.go files moved aside, the direct required lane exited 0 with 22 packages
reporting `[no test files]` (PR#6 VERIFY, FINDING 3). These floors are what make
that red. They are a FLOOR, not an expected count: they exist to catch a suite
being emptied or a package disappearing, not to pin an exact number.
Measured on 5eb2829 + this branch, go1.27.1, darwin/arm64, `go test -count=1 -json`:
of which internal/integration               45 tests (31 top-level + 14 subtests)
The integration suite is a SUPERSET of the unit suite — the build tag only ADDS
files — so its whole-suite floor says little about the integration tests
themselves. min_package_tests is what makes internal/integration's absence red:
emptying it costs ~4% of the total and would clear a suite floor comfortably.
Lowering a floor, or adding an allowed_skips entry, is a REVIEWED diff. An empty
allowed_skips is the correct state: a required test that is skipped is not a pass
(AGENTS.md). Both suites have zero skips today, and `make test-integration` FAILS
rather than skipping when its services are absent, so there is nothing to allow.
